body.input: It's an assistant that uses videos as a basic element of information.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: OK, so what practically should people do to try to fight against abuses of these algorithms or algorithms that manipulate us?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Honestly, it's a very, very difficult problem because to start with, there is very little public awareness of these issues.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Very few people would think there's anything wrong with their new algorithm, even though there is actually something wrong already,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: which is that it's trying to maximize engagement most of the time, which has very negative side effects.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So ideally, the very first thing is to stop trying to purely maximize engagement, try to propagate content based on popularity.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Instead, take into account the goals and the profiles of each user.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So you will be one example is, for instance, when I look at topic recommendations on Twitter,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: like they have this news tab with recommendations, it's always the worst garbage because it's content that appeals to the.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: The smallest common denominator to all Twitter users because they're trying to optimize, they're purely trying to obtain popularity,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: they're purely trying to optimize engagement, but that's not what I want.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So they should put me in control of some setting so that I define what's the objective function that Twitter is going to be following to show me this content.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So and honestly, so this is all about interface design.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And we are not. It's not realistic to give users control of a bunch of knobs that define algorithm.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Instead, we should purely put them in charge of defining the objective function.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Like let the user tell us what they want to achieve, how they want this algorithm to impact their lives.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So do you think it is that or do they provide individual article by article reward structure where you give a signal?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: I'm glad I saw this or I'm glad I didn't.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So like a Spotify type feedback mechanism, it works to some extent.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: I'm kind of skeptical about it because the only way the algorithm the algorithm will attempt to relate your choices with the choices of everyone else,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: which might, you know, if you have an average profile, that works fine.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: I'm sure Spotify accommodations work fine if you just like mainstream stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: If you don't, it can be it's not optimal at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: It'll be an inefficient search for the for the part of the Spotify world that represents you.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So it's a tough problem, but do note that even even a feedback system like what Spotify has does not give me control over.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Why the algorithm is trying to optimize.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Well, public awareness, which is what we're doing now, is a good place to start.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Do you have concerns about long term existential threats of artificial intelligence?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Well, as I was saying, our world is increasingly made of information.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: AI algorithms are increasingly going to be our interface to this world of information.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And somebody will be in control of these algorithms.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And that puts us in any kind of bad situation.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Right. It has risks.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: It has risks coming from potentially large companies wanting to optimize their own goals, maybe profit, maybe something else.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Also from governments who might want to use these algorithms as a means of control of the population.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Do you think there's existential threat that could arise from that?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So existential threats.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So maybe you're referring to the singularity narrative where robots just take over.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Well, I don't not terminate a robots and I don't believe it has to be a singularity.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: We're just talking to, just like you said, the algorithm controlling masses of populations.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: The existential threat being hurt ourselves much like a nuclear war would hurt ourselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: That kind of thing. I don't think that requires a singularity.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: That requires a loss of control over AI algorithms.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Yes. So I do agree there are concerning trends.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Honestly, I wouldn't want to make any long term predictions.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: I don't think today we really have the capability to see what the dangers of AI are going to be in 50 years, in 100 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: I do see that we are already faced with concrete and present dangers surrounding the negative side effects of content recommendation systems,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: of newsfeed algorithms concerning algorithmic bias as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So we are delegating more and more decision processes to algorithms.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Some of these algorithms are uncrafted. Some are learned from data.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: But we are delegating control. Sometimes it's a good thing, sometimes not so much.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And there is in general very little supervision of this process.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So we are still in this period of very fast change, even chaos, where society is restructuring itself,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: turning into an information society, which itself is turning into an increasingly automated information processing society.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And well, yeah, I think the best we can do today is try to raise awareness around some of these issues.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And I think we're actually making good progress.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: If you look at algorithmic bias, for instance, three years ago, even two years ago, very, very few people were talking about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And now all the big companies are talking about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: They are often not in a very serious way, but at least it is part of the public discourse.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: You see people in Congress talking about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So and it all started from raising awareness.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Right. So in terms of alignment problem, trying to teach as we allow algorithms, just even recommender systems on Twitter,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: encoding human values and morals, decisions that touch on ethics.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: How hard do you think that problem is?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: How do we have loss functions in neural networks that have some component, some fuzzy components of human morals?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Well, I think this is really all about objective function engineering, which is probably going to be increasingly a topic of concern in the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Like for now, we're just using very naive loss functions because the hard part is not actually what you're trying to minimize.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: It's everything else, but as the everything else is going to be increasingly automated,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: we're going to be focusing our human attention on increasingly high level components,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: like what's actually driving the whole learning system, like the objective function.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So loss function engineering is going to be loss function engineer is probably going to be a job title in the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And then the tooling you're creating with Keras essentially takes care of all the details underneath and basically the human expert is needed for exactly that.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: That's the idea. Keras is the interface between the data you're collecting and the business goals.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And your job as an engineer is going to be to express your business goals and your understanding of your business or your product,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: your system as a kind of loss function or kind of set of constraints.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Does the possibility of creating an AGI system excite you or scare you or bore you?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So intelligence can never really be general.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: You know, at best it can have some degree of generality like human intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: It's also always as some specialization in the same way that human intelligence is specialized in a certain carrier of problems, is specialized in the human experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And when people talk about AGI, I'm never quite sure if they're talking about very, very smart AI, so smart that it's even smarter than humans,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: or they're talking about human like intelligence because these are different things.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Let's say, presumably, I'm impressing you today with my humanness.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So imagine that I was in fact a robot. So what does that mean?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: I'm impressing you with natural language processing.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Maybe if you weren't able to see me, maybe this is a phone call.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So that kind of system.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Okay, so.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Companion.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So that's very much about building human like AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And you're asking me, you know, is this an exciting perspective?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: I think so, yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Not so much because of what artificial human like intelligence could do, but, you know, from an intellectual perspective, I think if you could build truly human like intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: that means you could actually understand human intelligence, which is fascinating, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Human like intelligence is going to require emotions, it's going to require consciousness, which is not things that would normally be required by an intelligent system.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: If you look at, you know, we were mentioning earlier, like science as a superhuman problem solving agent or system, it does not have consciousness, it doesn't have emotions.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: In general, so emotions, I see consciousness as being on the same spectrum as emotions.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: It is a component of the subjective experience that is meant very much to guide behavior generation, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: It's meant to guide your behavior.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Including in a social context, so that's why we actually need emotions, that's why we need consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: An artificial intelligence system developed in a different context may well never need them, may well never be conscious, like science.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Well, on that point, I would argue it's possible to imagine that there's echoes of consciousness in science when viewed as an organism, that science is consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So, I mean, how would you go about testing this hypothesis?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: How do you probe the subjective experience of an abstract system like science?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Well, the point of probing any subjective experience is impossible because I'm not science, I'm Lex.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So I can't probe another entities, another, it's no more than bacteria on my skin.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: You're Lex, I can ask you questions about your subjective experience and you can answer me and that's how I know you're conscious.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Yes, but that's because we speak the same language.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: You perhaps, we have to speak the language of science in order to ask.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Honestly, I don't think consciousness, just like emotions of pain and pleasure, is not something that inevitably arises from any sort of sufficiently intelligent information processing.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: It is a feature of the mind and if you've not implemented it explicitly, it is not there.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So you think it's an emergent feature of a particular architecture.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So do you think?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: It's a feature in the same sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So again, the subjective experience is all about guiding behavior.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: If the problems you're trying to solve don't really involve an embodied agent, maybe in a social context, generating behavior and pursuing goals like this.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And if you get science, that's not really what's happening, even though it is a form of artificial AI, artificial intelligence in the sense that it is solving problems, it is accumulating knowledge, accumulating solutions and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So if you're not explicitly implementing a subjective experience, implementing certain emotions and implementing consciousness, it's not going to just spontaneously emerge.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: But human-like intelligence can only arise in a human-like context.

body.input: Intelligence is tired.

body.input: In other humans in order for you to demonstrate that you have human-like intelligence, essentially.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And the other is about the degree to which this intelligence is human-like.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: It's actually two different questions.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So if you look, you mentioned earlier the Turing test.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Well, I actually don't like the Turing test because it's very lazy.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: It's all about completely bypassing the problem of defining and measuring intelligence and instead delegating to a human judge or a panel of human judges.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So it's a total cop-out.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: If you want to measure how human-like an agent is, I think you have to make it interact with other humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Maybe it's not necessarily a good idea to have these other humans be the judges.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Maybe you should just observe behavior and compare it to what a human would actually have done.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: When it comes to measuring how smart, how clever an agent is and comparing that to the degree of human intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So we're already talking about two things, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: The degree, kind of like the magnitude of an intelligence and its direction, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Like the norm of a vector and its direction.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And the direction is like human likeness and the magnitude, the norm is intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: You could call it intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So the space of directions that are human-like is very narrow.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So the way you would measure the magnitude of intelligence in a system in a way that also enables you to compare it to that of a human.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Well, if you look at different benchmarks for intelligence today, they're all too focused on skill at a given task.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: That skill at playing chess, skill at playing Go, skill at playing Dota.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And I think that's not the right way to go about it because you can always beat a human at one specific task.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: The reason why our skill at playing Go or at juggling or anything is impressive is because we are expressing this skill within a certain set of constraints.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: If you remove the constraints, the constraints that we have one lifetime, that we have this body and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: If you remove the context, if you have unlimited trained data, if you can have access to, for instance, if you look at juggling, if you have no restriction on the hardware,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: then achieving arbitrary levels of skill is not very interesting and says nothing about the amount of intelligence you've achieved.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So if you want to measure intelligence, you need to rigorously define what intelligence is, which in itself, it's a very challenging problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Do you think that's possible?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: To define intelligence? Yes, absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: I mean, you can provide, many people have provided some definition.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: I have my own definition.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Where does your definition begin if it doesn't end?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Well, I think intelligence is essentially the efficiency with which you turn experience into generalizable programs.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So what that means is it's the efficiency with which you turn a sampling of experience space into the ability to process a larger chunk of experience space.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So measuring skill can be one proxy because many different tasks can be one proxy for measuring intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: But if you want to only measure skill, you should control for two things.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: You should control for the amount of experience that your system has and the priors that your system has.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: But if you control, if you look at two agents and you give them the same priors and you give them the same amount of experience,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: there is one of the agents that is going to learn programs, representation, something, a model,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: that will perform well on the larger chunk of experience space than the other.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And that is the smaller agent.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Yeah. So if you have fixed the experience, which generates better programs, better meaning more generalizable.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: That's really interesting. That's a very nice, clean definition of.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Oh, by the way, in this definition, it is already very obvious that intelligence has to be specialized because you're talking about experience space.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: You're talking about segments of experience space.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: You're talking about priors and you're talking about experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: All of these things define the context in which intelligence emerges.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And you can never look at the totality of experience space.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So intelligence has to be specialized.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: But it can be sufficiently large, the experience space, even though specialized,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: there's a certain point when the experience space is large enough to where it might as well be general.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: It feels general. It looks general.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: I mean, it's very relative.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Like, for instance, many people would say human intelligence is general.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: In fact, it is quite specialized.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: You know, we can definitely build systems that start from the same innate priors as what humans have at birth,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: because we already understand fairly well what sort of priors we have as humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Like many people have worked on this problem, most notably Elizabeth Spelka from Harvard.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: I don't know if you know her.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: She's worked a lot on what she calls core knowledge.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And it is very much about trying to determine and describe what priors we are born with.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Like language skills and so on, all that kind of stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So we have some pretty good understanding of what priors we are born with.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And so we could...

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So I've actually been working on a benchmark for the past couple of years, you know, on and off.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: I hope to be able to release it at some point.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: The idea is to measure the intelligence of systems by contouring for priors,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: contouring for amount of experience, and by assuming the same priors as what humans are born with,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: so that you can actually compare these scores to human intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And you can actually have humans pass the same test in a way that's fair.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And so importantly, such a benchmark should be such that any amount of practicing does not increase your score.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So try to picture a game where no matter how much you play this game,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: that does not change your skill at the game.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Can you picture that?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: As a person who deeply appreciates practice, I cannot actually.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: I cannot.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: There's actually a very simple trick.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So in order to come up with a task...

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So the only thing you can measure is skill at the task.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: All tasks are going to involve priors.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: The trick is to know what they are and to describe that.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And then you make sure that this is the same set of priors as what humans start with.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So you create a task that assumes these priors, that exactly documents these priors.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So that's the priors are made explicit and there are no other priors involved.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And then you generate a certain number of samples in experience space for this task.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And this for one task, assuming that the task is new for the agent passing it,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: that's one test of this definition of intelligence that we set up.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And now you can scale that to many different tasks.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: That each task should be new to the agent passing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And also should be human interpretable and understandable,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: so that you can actually have a human pass the same test.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And then you can compare the score of your machine and the score of your human.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Which could be a lot of...

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: You could even start a task like MNIST,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: just as long as you start with the same set of priors.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: The problem with MNIST humans are already trying to recognize digits.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: But let's say we're considering objects that are not digits,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: some complete arbitrary patterns.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Well, humans already come with visual priors about how to process that.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So in order to make the game fair, you would have to

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: isolate these priors and describe them and then express them as computational rules.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Having worked a lot with vision science people, that's exceptionally difficult.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: A lot of progress has been made. There's been a lot of good tests.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And basically reducing all of human vision into some good priors.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: We're still probably far away from that perfectly,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: but as a start for a benchmark, that's an exciting possibility.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Yeah. So Elisabeth Spelke actually lists objectness as one of the core knowledge priors.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Objectness. Cool.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Objectness. Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So we have priors about objectness, like about the visual

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: space, about time, about agents, about goal-oriented behavior.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: We have many different priors.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: But what's interesting is that, sure, we have this pretty diverse and rich set of priors,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: but it's also not that diverse.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: We are not born into this world with a ton of knowledge about the world,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: with only a small set of core knowledge.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Yeah, it's hard. Do you have a sense of how it feels to us humans that that set is not that large,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: but just even the nature of time that we kind of integrate pretty effectively through all

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: of our perception, all of our reasoning.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Maybe how, you know, do you have a sense of how easy it is to encode those priors?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Maybe it requires building a universe and then the human brain in order to encode those priors.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Or do you have a hope that it can be listed like an axiomatic system?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: I don't think so. So you have to keep in mind that any knowledge about the world that we are born with

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: is something that has to have been encoded into our DNA by evolution at some point.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And DNA is a very, very low bandwidth medium.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Like it's extremely long and expensive to encode anything into DNA because first of all,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: you need some sort of evolutionary pressure to guide this writing process.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And then, you know, the higher level information you're trying to write,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: the longer it's going to take.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: And the thing in the environment that you're trying to encode knowledge about has to be stable

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: over this duration. So you can only encode into DNA things that constitute an evolutionary advantage.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So this is actually a very small subset of all possible knowledge about the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: You can only encode things that are stable, that are true over very, very long periods of time,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: typically millions of years. For instance, we might have some visual priors about

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: the shape of snakes, right? But all the, what makes a face,

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: what's the difference between a face and an around face. But consider this interesting question.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Do we have any innate sense of the visual difference between a male face and a female face?

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: What do you think? For human, I mean.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: I would have to look back into evolutionary history when the genders emerged, but yeah, most...

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: I mean, the faces of humans are quite different from the faces of great apes.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Great apes, right? Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: That's interesting, but yeah. You couldn't tell the face of a female

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: chimpanzee from the face of a male chimpanzee, probably.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: Yeah, and I don't think us humans have all that ability.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: So we do have innate knowledge of what makes a face, but it's actually impossible for us to have

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

body.input: any DNA encoded knowledge of the difference between a female human face and a male human face.

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

metadata.title: Podcast: François Chollet: Keras, Deep Learning, and the Progress of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #38

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: It's just asking it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: All right, well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: What do you think a robot is?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: What I think a robot is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: is something that has some level of intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: and some level of magic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: That little shine in the eye, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: that allows you to navigate the uncertainty of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: So that means like autonomous vehicles to me in that sense

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: are robots because they navigate the uncertainty,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: the complexity of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: Obviously social robots are that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: I love that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: I like that you mentioned magic because that also,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: well, so first of all,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: I don't define robot definitively in the book

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: because there is no definition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: There's no definition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: That's what everyone agrees on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: And if you look back through time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: people have called things robots until they lose the magic

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: because they're more ubiquitous.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: Like a vending machine used to be called a robot

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: and now it's not, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: So I do agree with you that there's this magic aspect

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: that which is how people understand robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: If you ask a roboticist,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: they have the definition of something that is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: well, it has to be physical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: Usually it's not an AI agent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: It has to be embodied.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: They'll say it has to be able to sense its environment

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: in some way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: It has to be able to make a decision autonomously

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: and then act on its environment again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: I think that's a pretty good technical definition

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: even though it really breaks down

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: when you come to things like the smartphone

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: because the smartphone can do all of those things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: And most robotists would not call it a robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: So there's really no one good definition

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: but part of why I wrote the book

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: is because people have a definition of robot in their minds

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: that is usually very focused

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: on a comparison of robots to humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: So if you Google image search robot,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: you get a bunch of humanoid robots,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: robots with a torso and head and two arms and two legs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: And that's the definition of robot

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: that I'm trying to get us away from

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: because I think that it trips us up a lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: Why does the humanoid form trip us up a lot?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: Well, because this constant comparison of robots to people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: artificial intelligence to human intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: first of all, it doesn't make sense

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: from a technical perspective

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: because the early AI researchers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: some of them were trying to recreate human intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: Some people still are and there's a lot to be learned

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: from that academically, et cetera.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: But that's not where we've ended up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: AI doesn't think like people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: We wind up in this fallacy

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: where we're comparing these two and when we talk

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: about what intelligence even is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: we're often comparing to our own intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: And then the second reason this bothers me

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: is because it doesn't make sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: I just think it's boring to recreate intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: that we already have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: I see the scientific value

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: of understanding our own intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: but from a practical,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: what could we use these technologies for perspective,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: it's much more interesting to create something new,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: to create a skillset that we don't have

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: that we can partner with in what we're trying to achieve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: And it should be in some deep ways similar to us,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: but in most ways different

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: because you still want to have a connection,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: which is why the similarity might be necessary.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: That's what people argue, yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: And I think that's true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: So the two arguments for humanoid robots are,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: people need to be able to communicate

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: and relate to robots,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: and we relate most of things that are like ourselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: And we have a world that's built for humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: So we have stairs and narrow passageways and door handles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: And so we need humanoid robots to be able to navigate that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: And so you're speaking to the first one,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: which is absolutely true,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: but what we know from social robotics

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: and a lot of human robot interaction research is that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: all you need is something that's enough like a person

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: to, for it to give off cues that someone relates to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: And that, but that doesn't have to look human

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: or even act human.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: You can take a robot like R2-D2

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: and it just like beeps and boops

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: and people love R2-D2, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: Even though it's just like a trash can on wheels.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: And they like R2-D2 more than C3PO, who's a humanoid.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: So there's lots of ways to make robots even better

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: than humans in some ways and make us relate more to them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: Yeah, it's kind of amazing the variety of cues

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: that can be used to anthropomorphize the thing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: like a glowing orb or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: Just a voice, just subtle basic interaction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: I think people sometimes over engineer these things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: Like simplicity can go a really long way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: Totally.

body.input: Yeah.

body.input: Yeah.

body.input: Versus like roboticists.

body.input: Roboticists, quote unquote, are mostly clueless.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: It seems like.

body.input: They just have their own discipline

body.input: that they're very good at and they don't have.

body.input: Yeah, but that don't, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: I feel like robotics of the early 21st century

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: is not going to be the robotics of the later 21st century.

body.input: Like if you call yourself a roboticist,

body.input: it'd be something very different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: Because I think more and more,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: you'd be like a, maybe like a control engineer or something,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: controls engineer, like you separate

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: because ultimately all the unsolved,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: And that's why, but like, I think you're so right

body.input: Because for me, I just, we've had robots for so long

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: and they've just been behind the scenes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: So I think that the goal is not to discourage

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329
