metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: that people won't think are sentient.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: I don't think that's possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: I think you're right, this is coming.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: It's something that we have to acknowledge

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: and even embrace and be very aware of.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: So one of the really interesting perspectives

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: that your book takes on a system like this

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: Can you kind of try to, again, sneak up,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: Yeah, and it gets trickier with the language stuff,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: but we'll get into that too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: I think that animals are a really great thought experiment

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: when we're thinking about AI and robotics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: because again, this comparing them to humans

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: that leads us down the wrong path,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: both because it's not accurate,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: but also I think for the future, we don't want that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: We want something that's a supplement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: But I think animals, because we've used them

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: throughout history for so many different things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: we domesticated them not because they do what we do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: And it's just like, whether we're talking about companionship,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: whether we're talking about work integration,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: there's just so many things we can draw on in that history

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: from these entities that can sense, think,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: make autonomous decisions and learn

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: that are applicable to how we should be thinking

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: about robots and AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: And the point of the book is not that they're the same thing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: that animals and robots are the same.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: But the point is that-

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: I do it all the time.

body.input: Oh really?

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: Like if it was a giant squirrel,

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: Yeah, I mean, people point to the fact

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: And so they, evolutionary biologists think that dogs evolved

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

body.input: to be more appealing to us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

metadata.title: Podcast: Kate Darling: Social Robots, Ethics, Privacy and the Future of MIT | Lex Fridman Podcast #329

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: just on fear, because it's so fascinating, is have you learned anything about what it takes to

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: overcome fears? Yes. And that comes from two, from a research study standpoint,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: two parallel tracks of research. One was done actually in mice, because we have a mouse lab

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: also where we can probe around in different brain areas and try and figure out what interesting

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: brain areas we might want to probe around in humans. And a graduate student in my lab,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: she's now at Caltech, Lindsay Soleil, published a paper back in 2018 showing that when we're

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: at first, it might seem a little bit obvious, but the mechanisms are not, which is that there are

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: really three responses to fear. You can pause, you can freeze essentially, you can retreat,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: you can back up, or you can go forward. And there's a single hub of neurons in the midbrain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: actually not the midbrain, but it's in the middle of the thalamus, which is a forebrain structure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: And depending on which neurons are active there, there's a much higher probability that a mouth

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: or it turns out, or a human will advance in the face of fear or will pause or will retreat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: Now that just assigns a neural structure to a behavioral phenomenon. But what's interesting

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: is that it turns out that the lowest level of stress or autonomic arousal is actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: associated with the pausing and freezing response. Then as the threat becomes more impending,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: and we used visual looms in this case, the retreat response has a slightly higher level

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: of autonomic arousal and stress. So think about playing hide and go seek and you're trying to

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: stay quiet in a closet that you're hiding. If you're very calm, it's easy to stay quiet and still.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: As your level of stress goes up, it's harder to maintain that level of quiet and stillness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: You see this also in animals that are stalking. A cat will chatter its teeth. That's actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: sort of top-down inhibition and trying to restrain behavior. So the freeze response

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: is actually an active response, but it's fairly low stress. And what was interesting to us is

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: that the highest level of autonomic arousal was associated with the forward movement toward the

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: threat. So in your case, jumping out of the plane. However, the forward movement in the face of

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: threat was linked to the activation of what we call collateral, which means just a side connection,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: literally a wire in the brain that connects to the dopamine circuits for reward. And so when one

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: safely and adaptively, meaning you survive, moves through a threat or toward a threat,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: it's rewarded as a positive experience. And so the key, it actually maps very well the cognitive

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: behavioral therapy and a lot of the existing treatments for trauma is that you have to confront

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: the thing that makes you afraid. So otherwise you exist in this very low level of reverberatory

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: circuit activity where the circuits for autonomic arousal are humming and they're humming more and

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: more and more. And we have to remember that stress and fear and threat were designed to agitate us

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: so that we actually move. So the reason I mention this is I think a lot of times people think that

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: the maximum stress response or fear response is to freeze and to lock up. But that's actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: not the maximum stress response. The maximum stress response is to advance, but it's associated with

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: reward. It has positive valence. So there's this kind of, everyone always thinks about the bell

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: increases, performance goes higher and then it drops off as you get really stressed. But there's

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: another bump further out that's distribution where you perform very well under very high levels of

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: stress. And so we've been spending a lot of time in humans and in animals exploring what it takes

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: to get people comfortable to go to that place and also to let them experience how their heightened

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: states of cognition there. There's changes in time perception that allow you to evaluate your

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: like, what's the meaning of life is, um, I think illustrated best by the Victor Franco example,

body.input: although there are other examples too, which is that our sense of meaning is very elastic

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: in time and space. And I'm, um, uh, we talked a little bit about this earlier, but it's amazing

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: to me that somebody locked in a cell or a concentration camp can bring the horizon in

body.input: close enough that they can then micro slice their environment so that they can find rewards and

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: think this is really speaks to one of the most important features of the human mind, which is

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: we could do, let's take two opposite extremes. One would be, let's say the alarm went off right

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: all that would matter. The only meaning would be get out of here, safe, figure out what's going on,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: contact loved ones, et cetera. If we were to sit back totally relaxed, we could do the, you know,

body.input: what is it? I think it's called pale blue dot thing or whatever, where we could imagine ourselves

body.input: in this room and then they were in the United States and this continent and the earth and then

body.input: meaningless, right? If you see yourself as just one brief glimmer in all of time and all of space,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: you go to, I don't matter. And if you go to, oh, every little thing that happens in this text

body.input: thread or this, you know, comment section on YouTube or Instagram, your space time bubble is tiny,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: then everything seems inflated and the brain will contract and dilate its space time

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: vision and time, but also sense of meaning. And that's beautiful. And it's what allows us

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: to be so dynamic in different environments and we can pull from the past and the present and future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: It's why examples like Nelson Mandela and Viktor Frankl had to include, it makes sense that it

body.input: wasn't just about grinding it out. They had to find those dopamine rewards even in those little

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: boxes they were forced into. So I'm not trying to dodge an answer, but for me personally, and I

body.input: think about this a lot because I have this complicated history in science where my undergraduate,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: graduate advisor and postdoctoral advisor all died young. So, you know, and they were wonderful

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: the thing that we're experiencing holding tremendous meaning, but it only holds that

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: gives meaning is the understanding that you can move between these different space time

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

body.input: about the cosmos in saying that. It's really the fact that sometimes we say and do and think

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Huberman: Neuroscience of Optimal Performance | Lex Fridman Podcast #139

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: I think planaria hold the answer to pretty much every deep question of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: For one thing, they're similar to our ancestors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So they have true symmetry, they have a true brain, they're not like earthworms, they're

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: much more advanced life form.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: They have lots of different internal organs, but they're these little, they're about maybe

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: two centimeters in the centimeter to two in size.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: They have a head and a tail.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And the first thing is planaria are immortal, so they do not age.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: There's no such thing as an old planarian.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So that right there tells you that these theories of thermodynamic limitations on lifespan are

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: It's not that well over time of everything degrades.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: No, planaria can keep it going for probably how long if they've been around 400 million

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So the planaria in our lab are actually in physical continuity with planaria that were

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: here 400 million years ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: The following is a conversation with Michael Levin, one of the most fascinating and brilliant

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: biologists I've ever talked to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: He and his lab at Tufts University works on novel ways to understand and control complex

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: pattern formation in biological systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Andre Karpathy, a world-class AI researcher, is the person who first introduced me to Michael

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Levin's work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: I bring this up because these two people make me realize that biology has a lot to teach

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: us about AI, and AI might have a lot to teach us about biology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: This is the Lex Friedman podcast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: To support it, please check out our sponsors in the description.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And now, dear friends, here's Michael Levin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Embryogenesis is the process of building the human body from a single cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: I think it's one of the most incredible things that exists on Earth from a single embryo.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So how does this process work?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Yeah, it is an incredible process.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: I think it's maybe the most magical process there is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: I think one of the most fundamentally interesting things about it is that it shows that each

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: of us takes the journey from so-called just physics to mind, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Because we all start life as a single quiescent, unfertilized oocyte, and it's basically a

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: bag of chemicals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And you look at that and you say, okay, this is chemistry and physics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And then nine months and some years later, you have an organism with high level cognition

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: and preferences and inner life and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And what embryogenesis tells us is that that transformation from physics to mind is gradual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: It's smooth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: There is no special place where a lightning bolt says, boom, now you've gone from physics

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: to true cognition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: That doesn't happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And so we can see in this process that the whole mystery, the biggest mystery of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: universe basically, how you get mind from matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: From just physics in quotes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So where's the magic into the thing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: How do we get from information encoding DNA and make physical reality out of that information?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So one of the things that I think is really important if we're going to bring in DNA into

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: this picture is to think about the fact that what DNA encodes is the hardware of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: DNA contains the instructions for the kind of micro level hardware that every cell gets

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: to play with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So all the proteins, all the signaling factors, the ion channels, all the cool little pieces

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: of hardware that cells have, that's what's in the DNA.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: The rest of it is in so-called generic laws.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And these are laws of mathematics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: These are laws of computation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: These are laws of physics, of all kinds of interesting things that are not directly in

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: the DNA.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And that process, I think the reason I always put just physics in quotes is because I don't

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: think there is such a thing as just physics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: I think that thinking about these things in binary categories, like this is physics, this

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: is true cognition, this is as if it's only faking, these kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: I think that's what gets us in trouble.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: I think that we really have to understand that it's a continuum and we have to work

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: up the scaling, the laws of scaling, and we can certainly talk about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: There's a lot of really interesting thoughts to be had there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So the physics is deeply integrated with the information.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So the DNA doesn't exist on its own.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: The DNA is integrated in some sense in response to the laws of physics at every scale.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: The laws of the environment it exists in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Yeah, the environment and also the laws of the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: I mean, the thing about the DNA is that once evolution discovers a certain kind of machine,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: that if the physical implementation is appropriate, it's sort of, and this is hard to talk about

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: because we don't have a good vocabulary for this yet, but it's a very kind of platonic

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: notion that if the machine is there, it pulls down interesting things that you do not have

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: to evolve from scratch because the laws of physics give it to you for free.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So just as a really stupid example, if you're trying to evolve a particular triangle, you

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: can evolve the first angle and you evolve the second angle, but you don't need to evolve

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: the third.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: You know what it is already.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Now, why do you know?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: That's a gift for free from geometry in a particular space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: You know what that angle has to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And if you evolve an ion channel, which is ion channels are basically transistors, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: They're voltage gated current conductances.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: If you evolve that ion channel, you immediately get to use things like truth tables.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: You get logic functions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: You don't have to evolve the logic function.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: You don't have to evolve a truth table.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: It doesn't have to be in the DNA.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: You get it for free, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And the fact that if you have NAND gates, you can build anything you want, you get that

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: for free.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: All you have to evolve is that first step, that first little machine that enables you

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: to couple to those laws.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And there's laws of adhesion and many other things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And this is all that interplay between the hardware that's set up by the genetics and

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: the software that's made, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: The physiological software that basically does all the computation and the cognition

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: and everything else is a real interplay between the information and the DNA and the laws of

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: physics of computation and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So is it fair to say just like this idea that the laws of mathematics are discovered, they're

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: latent within the fabric of the universe in that same way the laws of biology are kind

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: of discovered?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Yeah, I think that's absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And it's probably not a popular view, but I think that's right on the money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Well, I think that's a really deep idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And embryogenesis is the process of revealing, of embodying, of manifesting these laws.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: You're not building the laws.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: You're just creating the capacity to reveal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: I think, again, not the standard view of molecular biology by any means, but I think that's right

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: on the money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: I'll give you a simple example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Some of our latest work with these xenobots, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So what we've done is to take some skin cells off of an early frog embryo and basically

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: ask about their plasticity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: If we give you a chance to reboot your multicellularity in a different context, what would you do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Because what you might assume by looking at the thing about embryogenesis is that it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: super reliable, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: It's very robust.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And that really obscures some of its most interesting features.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: We get used to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: We get used to the fact that acorns make oak trees and frog eggs make frogs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And we say, well, what else is it going to make?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: That's what it makes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: That's a standard story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: But the reality is, and so you look at these skin cells and you say, well, what do they

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: know how to do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Well, they know how to be a passive, boring, two-dimensional outer layer keeping the bacteria

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: from getting into the embryo.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: That's what they know how to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Well, it turns out that if you take these skin cells and you remove the rest of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: embryo, so you remove all of the rest of the cells and you say, well, you're by yourself

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: now, what do you want to do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So what they do is they form this little, this multi little creature that runs around

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: the dish.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: They have all kinds of incredible capacities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: They navigate through mazes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: They have various behaviors that they do both independently and together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: They basically, they implement von Neumann's dream of self-replication because if you sprinkle

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: a bunch of loose cells into the dish, what they do is they run around, they collect those

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: cells into little piles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: They sort of mush them together until those little piles become the next generation of

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: xenobots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So you've got this machine that builds copies of itself from loose material in its environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: None of this are things that you would have expected from the frog genome.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: In fact, the genome is wild type.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: There's nothing wrong with their genetics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Nothing has been added, no nanomaterials, no genomic editing, nothing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And so what we have done there is engineered by subtraction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: What you've done is you've removed the other cells that normally basically bully these

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: cells into being skin cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And you find out that what they really want to do is to be this, they want their default

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: behaviors to be a xenobot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: But in vivo, in the embryo, they get told to be skinned by these other cell types.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And so now here comes this really interesting question that you just posed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: When you ask where does the form of the tadpole and the frog come from, the standard answer

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: is well, it's selection.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So over millions of years, it's been shaped to produce the specific body that's fit for

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: froggy environments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Where does the shape of the xenobot come from?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: There's never been any xenobots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: There's never been selection to be a good xenobot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: These cells find themselves in the new environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: In 48 hours, they figure out how to be an entirely different protoorganism with new

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: capacities like kinematic self-replication.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: That's not how frogs or tadpoles replicate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: We've made it impossible for them to replicate their normal way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Within a couple of days, these guys find a new way of doing it that's not done anywhere

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: else in the biosphere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Well, actually, let's step back and define what are xenobots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So a xenobot is a self-assembling little protoorganism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: It's also a biological robot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Those things are not distinct.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: It's a member of both classes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: How much is it biology?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: How much is it robot?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: At this point, most of it is biology because what we're doing is we're discovering natural

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: behaviors of the cells and also of the cell collectives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: One of the really important parts of this was that we're working together with Josh

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Bongard's group at University of Vermont.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: They're computer scientists who do AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: They've basically been able to use a simulated evolution approach to ask, how can we manipulate

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: these cells, give them signals, not rewire their DNA, so not hardware, but experience

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: as signals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So can we remove some cells?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Can we add some cells?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Can we poke them in different ways to get them to do other things?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So in the future, there's going to be, we're now, and this is future unpublished work,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: but we're doing all sorts of interesting ways to reprogram them to new behaviors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: But before you can start to reprogram these things, you have to understand what their

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: innate capacities are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So that means engineering, programming, you're engineering them in the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And in some sense, the definition of a robot is something you in part engineer versus evolve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: I mean, it's such a fuzzy definition anyway, in some sense, many of the organisms within

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: our body are kinds of robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And I think robots is a weird line because it's, we tend to see robots as the other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: I think there will be a time in the future when there's going to be something akin to

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: the civil rights movements for robots, but we'll talk about that later, perhaps.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Anyway.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So how do you, can we just linger on it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: How do you build a xenobot?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: What are we talking about here from, from whence does it start and how does it become

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: the glorious xenobot?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So just to take one step back, one of the things that a lot of people get stuck on is

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: they say, well, you know, engineering requires new DNA circuits or it requires new nanomaterials.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: You know what the thing is, we are now moving from old school engineering, which used passive

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: materials, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: That things like, you know, wood, metal, things like this, that basically the only thing you

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: could depend on is that they were going to keep their shape.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: That's it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: They don't do anything else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: It's on you as an engineer to make them do everything they're going to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And then there were active materials and now computation materials.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: This is a whole new era.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: These are agential materials.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: This is your, you're now collaborating with your substrate because your material has an

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: agenda.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: These cells have, you know, billions of years of evolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: They have goals, they have preferences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: They're not just going to sit where you put them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: That's hilarious that you have to talk your material into keeping its shape.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: That is exactly right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: That is exactly right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: That is stay there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: It's like getting a bunch of cats or something and trying to organize the shape out of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: It's funny.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: We're on the same page here because in the paper, this is, this is currently just been

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: accepted in nature by engineering.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: One of the figures I have is building a tower out of Legos versus dogs, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So think about the difference, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: If you build out of Legos, you have full control over where it's going to go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: But if somebody knocks it over, it's game over.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: With the dogs, you cannot just come and stack them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: They're not going to stay that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: But the good news is that if you train them, then somebody knocks it over, they'll get

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: right back up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So it's all right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So as an engineer, what you really want to know is what can I depend on this thing to

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: That's really, you know, a lot of people have definitions of robots as far as what they're

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: made of or how they got here, you know, design versus evolve, whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: I don't think any of that is useful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: I think as an engineer, what you want to know is how much can I depend on this thing to

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: do when I'm not around to micromanage it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: What level of dependency can I give this thing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: How much agency does it have?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Which then tells you what techniques do you use.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So do you use micromanagement?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Like you put everything where it goes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Do you train it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Do you give it signals?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Do you try to convince it to do things?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: How much, you know, how intelligent is your substrate?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And so now we're moving into this, into this area where you're, you're, you're working with

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: a gentile materials.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: That's a collaboration.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: That's not, that's not old, old style.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: What's the word you're using?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: A gentile?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: A gentile.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: What's that mean?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Agency.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: It comes from the word agency.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So, so basically the material has agency, meaning that it has some, some level of obviously

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: not human level, but some level of preferences, goals, memories, ability to remember things

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: to compute into the future, meaning anticipate, you know, when you're working with cells,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: they have all of that to some, to various degrees.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: Is that empowering or limiting having material that has a mind of its own, literally?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: I think it's both, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So it raises difficulties because it means that if you, if you're using the old mindset,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: which is a linear kind of extrapolation of what's going to happen, you're going to be

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: surprised and shocked all the time because biology does not do what we linearly expect

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: materials to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: On the other hand, it's massively liberating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And so in the following way, I've argued that advances in regenerative medicine require

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: us to take advantage of this because what it means is that you can get the material

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: to do things that you don't know how to micromanage.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: So just as a simple example, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: If you, if you, you had a rat and you wanted this rat to do a circus trick, put a ball

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: in the little hoop.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: You can do it the micromanagement way, which is try to control every neuron and try to

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: play the thing like a puppet, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And maybe someday that'll be possible, maybe, or you can train the rat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: And this is why humanity for thousands of years before we knew any neuroscience, we

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: had no idea what's between the ears of any animal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: We were able to train these animals because once you recognize the level of agency of

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: a certain system, you can use appropriate techniques.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: If you know the currency of motivation, reward and punishment, you know how smart it is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325

body.input: you know what kinds of things it likes to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Michael Levin: Biology, Life, Aliens, Evolution, Embryogenesis & Xenobots | Lex Fridman Podcast #325
